name: TS3USB30ERSWR
title: TS3USB30E: ESD-protected 480 Mbps USB 2.0 1:2 multiplexer/demultiplexer with single enable, UQFN-10 and VSSOP-10
summary: A two-pole, two-throw analog switch for USB data pairs: the common pair D+/D- connects to either D1+/D1- or D2+/D2-, chosen by S, and an active-low enable OE opens both paths. It runs from a 3 V to 4.3 V supply (2.7 V in the feature list), takes 1.8 V logic on its control pins, and its data pins stand 5.25 V with the supply off. On-resistance is 6 ohm typical, 10 ohm maximum, with 1400 MHz typical -3 dB bandwidth and 7.5 pF on-capacitance. Every pin carries ESD protection; the I/O pins take 15 kV human-body model to ground.
key_figures: 3 V to 4.3 V recommended; 2.7 V to 4.3 V in the features

circuits.title: Two USB controllers sharing one connector
circuits.description: A set-top-box or DSP processor talks to a USB 2.0 controller and a DVR or mass-storage controller. The first controller's pair goes to port 1 (D1+, D1-), the second's to port 2 (D2+, D2-), and the common pair D+/D- runs to one USB connector. S picks which controller reaches the connector; OE low enables the path. S and OE are to be pulled to VCC or GND so neither floats.
notes: The processor links to both controllers over their own buses. The part operates without external components; a bypass capacitor goes at VCC, as close to the pin as it can sit.

circuits.title: Turn-on and turn-off time
circuits.description: D is held at VIN = VCC. Each port pin, VOUT1 at 1D and VOUT2 at 2D, carries RL = 50 Ω and CL = 5 pF in parallel to ground. Pulse generators drive S (VSEL) and OE (VOE) between 0 and 1.8 V. tON and tOFF run from the control edge's 50 % point to the output's 90 % point.

operation.text: Two matched switch poles share one control: D+ and D- go together to port 1 (D1+, D1-) or port 2 (D2+, D2-). The paths are bidirectional, so one host can reach two devices or two hosts one device. The 1400 MHz bandwidth passes high-speed signals with little edge or phase distortion and little attenuation; bit-to-bit skew is low and channel-to-channel isolation high.

OE high puts both poles in high impedance regardless of S, which isolates the bus when it is idle and lowers current. With OE low, S low connects port 1 and S high connects port 2. Switching from S or OE takes at most 30 ns to turn on and 25 ns to turn off.

S and OE accept 1.8 V logic: VIH is 1.3 V minimum at VCC = 3 V to 3.6 V and 1.7 V at 4.3 V. Both should be pulled to VCC or to GND so the switch never takes an unintended position from a floating pin; an unused control input must sit at VCC or GND. Holding a control input at a TTL level such as 2.6 V raises supply current by up to 10 µA per input.
With VCC at 0 V the data pins stand up to 5.25 V and leak at most ±2 µA (IOFF); IOFF supports partial power-down operation. With VCC above 0 V the data pins are limited to VCC + 0.3 V.
The switch needs no external components to work. Unused signal pins are best tied to ground through 50 ohm so signals do not reflect back into the device. The USB 1.0, 1.1 and 2.0 design rules apply.

Power enters at VCC and is to meet the USB 1.0, 1.1 and 2.0 requirements. A bypass capacitor at the VCC pin, as close as it can go, filters low-frequency noise; the layout example uses an 0603 capacitor from VCC to a ground via.

Keep the bypass capacitor next to VCC but away from the D+ and D- traces. Run D+ and D- at equal lengths, no longer than 4 inches, with differential impedance matched to the cable's. Use few vias and corners; open up the clearance round a via that cannot be avoided; make a 90° turn as two 45° bends or an arc; avoid through-hole test points on the pair. Keep the pair away from crystals, oscillators, clock sources, switching regulators, mounting holes, magnetics and clocked ICs. Stubs should be avoided, and kept under 200 mm if one is needed. Route the pair over a continuous VCC or GND plane, never across a plane split or anti-etch; where crossing a split cannot be avoided, decouple enough. A board of at least four layers is advised: signal, ground, power, signal, with most signal traces on the top layer directly over a solid ground plane.

In the example the port 1 and port 2 traces leave the part from its top and bottom edges toward the two devices, the D+ and D- common lines and S and OE leave sideways toward the system, GND goes straight to a via into the ground plane, and VCC runs out to an 0603 capacitor whose far end drops to a ground via.
